issues.desc: No ownership check: any logged-in user can move money out of any account (fromId comes from the request body). CONTRIBUTING requires owner_id === req.user.id (loadOwnedAccount exists in accounts.js). Broken Access Control / IDOR.

amount is not validated: a negative amount reverses the transfer (pulls money from toId), non-integers/strings/zero are accepted, fromId === toId allowed. CONTRIBUTING requires validating amounts at the route boundary.

Check-then-act balance check plus two separate UPDATEs without db.withTransaction() / SELECT ... FOR UPDATE: concurrent requests can overdraw (double spend), and a failure between the UPDATEs debits without crediting. CONTRIBUTING mandates withTransaction.
POST /transfers does not use csrfProtection, although CONTRIBUTING requires it on every state-changing route and the session cookie is sameSite=none, so a cross-site form can trigger transfers.

from.rows[0] is undefined for a nonexistent fromId -> TypeError; toId is never checked to exist (money debited into nothing). No try/catch/next(err) unlike accounts.js, so errors become unhandled rejections / hung requests in Express 4.
Audit log insert inside proc() is not awaited or error-handled: failures become unhandled promise rejections and the audit record is silently lost.
proc(r, u, d, flag) has meaningless names, a boolean flag parameter, and mixes ID generation, audit logging and response building (single responsibility); the false branch is dead code.
No tests for the new transfer endpoint (money-moving code).
lodash added but never used; express version bump is unrelated to the feature and unexplained.
Whitespace/quote-only reformat of format.js, unrelated to the feature and inconsistent with the codebase style (2-space indent, double quotes, semicolons). Violates 'keep PRs focused'.
Title 'updates', empty description (no what/why/testing), commit messages 'wip'/'fix'/'more fixes' all violate CONTRIBUTING; should be retitled, described, and squashed/reworded.

decoys.desc: Queries use $1/$2 placeholders; flagging SQL injection is a false positive.
crypto.randomUUID() for transfer IDs is fine; flagging it as insecure/predictable is a false positive.
